## Summary

I implemented intermediate-layer output prediction and controllable dropout for uncertainty estimation, touching only source files.

### `deepchem/models/layers.py`
Added a new `SwitchedDropout(tf.keras.layers.Layer)` class. It takes a `rate` in the constructor and accepts two inputs in `call`: a tensor and a scalar switch. The effective rate is `rate * switch`, so a switch of `1.0` applies dropout at the given rate (with the standard `1/(1-rate)` scaling) and `0.0` passes the input through unchanged. Includes `get_config` for serialization.

### `deepchem/models/keras_model.py`
- **`_predict`** — added an `outputs` parameter. When provided (a Keras Tensor or list), it returns the numpy values of those internal tensors instead of the standard prediction outputs, skipping prediction-index filtering and transformers. Graph mode fetches them via `session.run`; eager mode builds a temporary `tf.keras.Model(model.inputs, outputs)`. Errors if `outputs` and `uncertainty` are requested together. Also fixed the result-accumulation to correctly handle multiple outputs across batches.
- **`predict_on_generator`**, **`predict`**, **`predict_on_batch`** — added the optional `outputs=None` argument, threaded through to `_predict`.
- **`default_generator`** — replaced the `predict` boolean with a `mode` string (default `'fit'`, plus `'predict'` and `'uncertainty'`), with a docstring so subclasses can yield mode-dependent inputs (e.g. a dropout switch). Updated `predict`/`predict_uncertainty` callers to pass `mode='predict'` / `mode='uncertainty'`.

### Subclass overrides (to stay consistent with the new signature)
Updated `default_generator` in `fcnet.py` (`MultitaskClassifier`, `MultitaskFitTransformRegressor`) and `robust_multitask.py` (`RobustMultitaskClassifier`) to use `mode` instead of `predict`, and `MultitaskFitTransformRegressor.predict_on_generator` to forward `outputs`.
